top.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
top.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

top.title: Arsenal edge stubborn Slavia in Champions League
top.description: Arsenal now have 10 points from four Champions League games (Michal Cizek) Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday. Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings. "We have to value the fact that it's very difficult to win away from home. We've done it against a really tough opponent, as we expected," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. "Two very different halves. The first one where we played at a really high level in terms of tempo, intensity, quality and clarity in what we had to do," he added. The Premier League champions were quick to take control of the game in chilly conditions in the Czech capital. Madueke reaped the rewards on nine minutes. Gyokeres controlled David Raya's long clearance with his chest and passed the ball instinctively to Madueke sprinting behind him down the right flank. Madueke left the Slavia back four behind him with ease and beat diving Ukrainian teenager Nazar Domchak in the Slavia goal with a low shot. Gyokeres, one of six changes in Mikel Arteta's starting line-up from Sunday's 1-0 win at Liverpool, made it 2-0 on 38 minutes. He beat Domchak with a neat shot off the far post after a one-two with Mikel Merino on the edge of the Slavia box. - 'Far from our standards' - Czech champions Slavia were sluggish throughout the first half, producing a single chance when skipper Tomas Holes fired wide from inside the box. But they stepped up their pace considerably in the second half to stave off a repeat of a 3-0 home loss to the Gunners in the competition exactly a year ago. Slavia's Polish midfielder Oskar Kubiak forced a diving save from Raya seconds into the second half. Gabriel Magalhaes and Raya cleared two headers off the goalline in quick succession with 15 minutes to go, while David Zima fired over the bar. Raya then forced a Kubiak header onto the post. Slavia scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute when David Jurasek's cross bounced through the Arsenal defence and Wiktor Nowak blasted the ball into the net from close range. "(We) scored two goals. It should have been three, four or five. We didn't make that gap," said Arteta. "Right from the beginning, we were extremely far from our standards and everything that we have to do... in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half." It was the 23rd straight game without a win for the hosts in the Champions League, taking them within one of equalling AEK Athens' all-time record from 1992-2006. frj/jc

top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect So, you thought Alexis Lafreniere was having a breakout season? Wait til you hear what his former New York Rangers teammate Adam Edstrom is doing in Nashville. Edstrom scored his sixth goal of the season on Tuesday night, helping the Predators upset the Carolina Hurricanes 4-1 in Music City. Those six goals already represent a new career high in just 15 games for the towering 6-foot-7 forward. That puts Edstrom on a 34-goal pace this season. His track record suggests that whopping 24.0 shooting percentage won’t last over a full season, not to mention that the oft-injured forward never played more than 51 games in an NHL season. But give credit where credit is do. The 26-year-old from Sweden certainly blossomed after the Rangers traded him to the Predators for a fifth-round pick in the 2026 NHL Draft. Edstrom scored 10 goals in 97 games over three seasons with the Rangers, topping out with five goals and nine points in 2024-25. However, Edstrom quickly gained the trust of Predators coach Andrew Brunette, who put him on the third line with center Jack Drury and a rotating host of forwards on the other wing. top.title: Two teams, one court: How the Spurs are blending tradition with a new era of entertainment
top.description: The Hype Squad and Silver Dancers celebrate a victory during the San Antonio Spurs vs. Phoenix Suns game on Wednesday October 14, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. (Photo by Tony Garcia/San Antonio Spurs) (Tony Garcia) The pom-poms are back, the stunts are flying, and two generations of Spurs entertainment are sharing the spotlight at Frost Bank Center. Eight years after the San Antonio Spurs disbanded their iconic Silver Dancers in favor of the coed Hype Squad, the franchise has brought the dancers back to perform alongside the Hype Squad rather than replace it. The result is a game-day dynamic that blends the Silver Dancers' traditional jazz and pom routines with the Hype Squad's hip-hop performances, breakdancing and high-flying stunts. For performers Grace Echterling and Elena Valdellon, the arrangement is about more than sharing the court. It's about building a new identity for Spurs entertainment while preserving the traditions that came before them. "It feels iconic," said Echterling, a Silver Dancer who spent last season with the Hype Squad. "We're bringing back the legacy, but we're doing it a little bit differently." The Silver Dancers were disbanded in May 2018 amid reports of a "lack of interest," making way for the Hype Squad, which debuted during the 2018-19 NBA season. ALSO READ: Spurs vs. Mavericks: How to watch the game, who's starting, who's out Jordan Mandelkorn, vice president of marketing, creative and retail for Spurs Sports & Entertainment, said the organization began exploring the possibility of reviving the Silver Dancers as an addition to its existing entertainment program. "We love the Hype Squad. We love what they bring to the games," Mandelkorn said. "But we also kind of started to have more conversations around whether or not it was a good time to bring back the Silver Dancers in addition to the Hype Squad, not a replacement of." Two teams, one Spurs family For Echterling, the Silver Dancers' return presented an unexpected opportunity. The Waco native began training at the Joffrey Ballet School at age 14. She spent her rookie season with the Hype Squad before learning the franchise was reviving its longtime dance team. Excited to return to her technical dance roots but reluctant to leave her teammates, Echterling auditioned for both groups and let the coaches determine where she would fit best. She was selected for the Silver Dancers. Valdellon, a California native entering her second season with the Hype Squad, has remained focused on stunts, a specialty she developed through years of cheerleading, including at Cal State Fullerton. "I think it's important that both teams understand that we bring different dynamics with Hype Squad and Silver Dancers," Valdellon said. Despite their different performance styles, the groups occasionally rehearse together, make joint community appearances and share responsibilities during games. top.description: It was largely business as usual in matchweek four of the Champions League as Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona kept on scoring and Arsenal and Bayern Munich returned to winning ways while remaining unbeaten. But the story of the round belonged to Como, who made history by beating Lens 9-1 away from home and equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game. Cesc Fabregas’s impressive side now sit fourth in the league phase standings, behind PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal. Meanwhile, there was a frustrating defeat for Liverpool at Fenerbahce , but Manchester United produced a stunning comeback to beat Roma and potentially save Michael Carrick’s job , with Matheus Cunha scoring twice on a remarkable night at Old Trafford. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. top.title: Micah Parsons believes patience in ACL recovery will pay off for Green Bay Packers
top.description: GREEN BAY – His family has been asking the question for weeks. There are flights to book, tickets to purchase, a celebration waiting for whenever Micah Parsons reaches the finish line in the most tumultuous chapter of his career. Everyone wants to know when he’ll play again. Parsons can’t escape the daily probes, not to his surgically reconstructed left knee, but the uncertainty of his first snaps. He’s batted them all away, just the same as he did surrounded by cameras and tape recorders inside Lambeau Field, an hour after his first practice since tearing his ACL . “I’m telling them, ‘I’ve still got two weeks of practice,’” the Green Bay Packers star edge defender said Nov. 4. “We just got to pay for last-minute flights. It is what it is. You can buy your flight, you can’t do last minute, that’s up to you. But I’m not going to pinpoint a day to disappoint anyone or give people expectations that I can’t meet. “So I’ve got to stack 20 days, and hopefully on that 21st day, I feel incredible.” The timing of that 21st day, the final in his window to return off the physically-unable-to-perform list, is impossible not to notice. Parsons can return anytime in the next three weeks after his first practice Nov. 4, reduced to only individual drills. But Packers coach Matt LaFleur already has said he expects Parsons to use most, if not all, of that ramp-up window. On the 21st day, the Packers will be playing at the Los Angeles Rams in a prime-time matchup on Thanksgiving eve. Quite the stage for one of the NFL’s most-electric players to re-debut. If Parsons is thinking that far ahead, he’s not about to show it. He’s learned what all players do going through an ACL rehab, that it is humbling, that nobody is immune to the uncompromising demands. nigeria.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
nigeria.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students. Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on. Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date. The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine. If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.” “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote. More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices. In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages. Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials. The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini. New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices. “We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP. The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy. In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.” “We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said. nigeria.title: Kekere-Ekun to chair presentation of Pinheiro’s 6 legal publications
nigeria.description: By Innocent Anaba The Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, will chair the public presentation of six legal books authored by Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, on November 20, 2026. The publications, which draw on Pinheiro’s nearly four decades of legal practice, examine critical areas of Nigerian law, including criminal litigation, arbitration, corporate insolvency, justice administration and emerging legal issues. The collection comprises Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide; Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure; Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria; Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One); The Compendium; and MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN. The book on criminal trials examines key procedural and evidential issues in criminal proceedings, including the treatment and admissibility of electronic evidence. Similarly, Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure explores the legal framework governing corporate rescue, restructuring and insolvency proceedings under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria examines the country’s arbitration framework, with particular attention to the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and the enforcement of arbitral awards. It also addresses the growing importance of alternative dispute resolution in settling commercial disputes. Beyond these practice-oriented publications, Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One) chronicles Pinheiro’s professional journey and experiences in the legal profession. The Compendium features scholarly essays by legal practitioners and academics, while MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN examines the intersection of law, faith and Nigeria’s plural legal system through contributions from various authors. The six publications bring together practical legal guidance, academic research and professional reflections on the development of Nigerian law, with subject matter relevant to judges, legal practitioners, academics and other stakeholders in the administration of justice. The public presentation, organised by Pinheiro LP, is expected to attract members of the judiciary, the Bar, academia and other stakeholders in the legal profession. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.” What the ruling does and does not do The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction. The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case. Bitcoin changed hands at $80,099 at 3:12 p.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.61 trillion and roughly $39.6 billion in trading volume over the past 24 hours. The low came in the 10 p.m. ET hour on Tuesday, as results showed Democrats taking both chambers. The high came in the 10 a.m. hour on Wednesday. That is a swing of about 7.3% from bottom to top in roughly 12 hours. The climb was a short squeeze. About $950 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and bets against prices made up $560 million of that. Bitcoin positions accounted for $403 million of the total, 76% of it shorts. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju wrote on X Wednesday afternoon that $215 million in bitcoin shorts were liquidated in a single hour. sports.title: Arsenal edge stubborn Slavia in Champions League
sports.description: Arsenal now have 10 points from four Champions League games (Michal Cizek) Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday. Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings. "We have to value the fact that it's very difficult to win away from home. We've done it against a really tough opponent, as we expected," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. "Two very different halves. The first one where we played at a really high level in terms of tempo, intensity, quality and clarity in what we had to do," he added. The Premier League champions were quick to take control of the game in chilly conditions in the Czech capital. Madueke reaped the rewards on nine minutes. Gyokeres controlled David Raya's long clearance with his chest and passed the ball instinctively to Madueke sprinting behind him down the right flank. Madueke left the Slavia back four behind him with ease and beat diving Ukrainian teenager Nazar Domchak in the Slavia goal with a low shot. Gyokeres, one of six changes in Mikel Arteta's starting line-up from Sunday's 1-0 win at Liverpool, made it 2-0 on 38 minutes. He beat Domchak with a neat shot off the far post after a one-two with Mikel Merino on the edge of the Slavia box. - 'Far from our standards' - Czech champions Slavia were sluggish throughout the first half, producing a single chance when skipper Tomas Holes fired wide from inside the box. But they stepped up their pace considerably in the second half to stave off a repeat of a 3-0 home loss to the Gunners in the competition exactly a year ago. Slavia's Polish midfielder Oskar Kubiak forced a diving save from Raya seconds into the second half. Gabriel Magalhaes and Raya cleared two headers off the goalline in quick succession with 15 minutes to go, while David Zima fired over the bar. Raya then forced a Kubiak header onto the post. Slavia scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute when David Jurasek's cross bounced through the Arsenal defence and Wiktor Nowak blasted the ball into the net from close range. "(We) scored two goals. It should have been three, four or five. We didn't make that gap," said Arteta. "Right from the beginning, we were extremely far from our standards and everything that we have to do... in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half." It was the 23rd straight game without a win for the hosts in the Champions League, taking them within one of equalling AEK Athens' all-time record from 1992-2006. frj/jc

sports.description: The Hype Squad and Silver Dancers celebrate a victory during the San Antonio Spurs vs. Phoenix Suns game on Wednesday October 14, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. (Photo by Tony Garcia/San Antonio Spurs) (Tony Garcia) The pom-poms are back, the stunts are flying, and two generations of Spurs entertainment are sharing the spotlight at Frost Bank Center. Eight years after the San Antonio Spurs disbanded their iconic Silver Dancers in favor of the coed Hype Squad, the franchise has brought the dancers back to perform alongside the Hype Squad rather than replace it. The result is a game-day dynamic that blends the Silver Dancers' traditional jazz and pom routines with the Hype Squad's hip-hop performances, breakdancing and high-flying stunts. For performers Grace Echterling and Elena Valdellon, the arrangement is about more than sharing the court. It's about building a new identity for Spurs entertainment while preserving the traditions that came before them. "It feels iconic," said Echterling, a Silver Dancer who spent last season with the Hype Squad. "We're bringing back the legacy, but we're doing it a little bit differently." The Silver Dancers were disbanded in May 2018 amid reports of a "lack of interest," making way for the Hype Squad, which debuted during the 2018-19 NBA season. ALSO READ: Spurs vs. Mavericks: How to watch the game, who's starting, who's out Jordan Mandelkorn, vice president of marketing, creative and retail for Spurs Sports & Entertainment, said the organization began exploring the possibility of reviving the Silver Dancers as an addition to its existing entertainment program. "We love the Hype Squad. We love what they bring to the games," Mandelkorn said. She spent her rookie season with the Hype Squad before learning the franchise was reviving its longtime dance team. Excited to return to her technical dance roots but reluctant to leave her teammates, Echterling auditioned for both groups and let the coaches determine where she would fit best. She was selected for the Silver Dancers. Valdellon, a California native entering her second season with the Hype Squad, has remained focused on stunts, a specialty she developed through years of cheerleading, including at Cal State Fullerton. "I think it's important that both teams understand that we bring different dynamics with Hype Squad and Silver Dancers," Valdellon said. Despite their different performance styles, the groups occasionally rehearse together, make joint community appearances and share responsibilities during games. sports.description: GREEN BAY – His family has been asking the question for weeks. There are flights to book, tickets to purchase, a celebration waiting for whenever Micah Parsons reaches the finish line in the most tumultuous chapter of his career. Everyone wants to know when he’ll play again. Parsons can’t escape the daily probes, not to his surgically reconstructed left knee, but the uncertainty of his first snaps. He’s batted them all away, just the same as he did surrounded by cameras and tape recorders inside Lambeau Field, an hour after his first practice since tearing his ACL . “I’m telling them, ‘I’ve still got two weeks of practice,’” the Green Bay Packers star edge defender said Nov. 4. “We just got to pay for last-minute flights. It is what it is. You can buy your flight, you can’t do last minute, that’s up to you. But I’m not going to pinpoint a day to disappoint anyone or give people expectations that I can’t meet. “So I’ve got to stack 20 days, and hopefully on that 21st day, I feel incredible.” The timing of that 21st day, the final in his window to return off the physically-unable-to-perform list, is impossible not to notice. Parsons can return anytime in the next three weeks after his first practice Nov. 4, reduced to only individual drills. But Packers coach Matt LaFleur already has said he expects Parsons to use most, if not all, of that ramp-up window. On the 21st day, the Packers will be playing at the Los Angeles Rams in a prime-time matchup on Thanksgiving eve. Quite the stage for one of the NFL’s most-electric players to re-debut. If Parsons is thinking that far ahead, he’s not about to show it. He’s learned what all players do going through an ACL rehab, that it is humbling, that nobody is immune to the uncompromising demands. sports.description: LIV Golf was founded in 2021, with its first season taking place the following year [Getty Images] LIV Golf is set to be wound down after its investor withdrew its support because the proposed new league failed to attract enough players. LIV had hoped BC Partners Credit would provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing in April , leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September. The funding could have helped the competition move forward in a new form, dubbed LIV 2.0, but BC Partners is understood to have decided it is not viable to pursue a deal. While leading players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia had already walked away, BBC Sport understands that those working on LIV 2.0 had received commitments from co-investors, felt support from within the golf ecosystem and had around 30 players signed up, including major winners. But sources say the timelines ultimately proved insurmountable and they could not get the agreements they needed to move forward. The league had been facing a deadline to show it had enough player support to continue in 2027. The expectation is that an attorney acting for LIV will announce in a court hearing on Thursday that the proposal for LIV 2.0 is not viable. LIV aimed to 'destroy the European Tour' - McIlroy Westwood 'unemployed' amid LIV uncertainty as Rahm discusses exit What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival? How did we get here? LIV Golf has provided one of the most tumultuous episodes in the history of golf since its launch in 2021, one which threatened to tear the sport apart. High-profile players joined and were banned from other tours, as well as events such as the Ryder Cup. More than $5bn (£3.7bn) was spent by PIF, with major winners including Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau lured by lucrative contracts and vast prize money. But the future of the concept - and its star players - has been shrouded in uncertainty this year after the 2026 season ended early. An event on 26 August in Indianapolis proved to be the last. When PIF announced it was withdrawing its funding in April, LIV announced a "strategic evolution" - including a newly established independent board - and attempted to find replacement financial investors. The exodus of players continued, however, including the exits of Rahm, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell. When Rahm left it was reported he was owed about $100m (£75m) from the remainder of the contract. technology.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
technology.description: If you share content using public iCloud links, Apple could soon be looking over your shoulder and checking for "harmful content." The iBiz announced plans to moderate publicly accessible iCloud share links in version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS on a support page published on Tuesday. To clarify, this applies only to iCloud content shared via links created to be accessible to anyone, as opposed to content shared directly with other people. “Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content,” Apple explained on the new help page without bothering to define what harmful content means. Based on the wording, it appears those checks will apply to all iCloud items shared using "Anyone with the Link," which Apple says it can also access. The company hasn't explained how the checks will work. The share-with-anyone option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, Apple said, even if Advanced Data Protection , Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled for the account. “If you try to upload harmful content, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete the content at any time,” the help page continues, adding that the iMaker may also block or disable accounts associated with harmful content. The company also said it reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary, suggesting that its undefined "harmful content" category could include child sexual abuse material (CSAM), malware, and other potentially unlawful content. Without a proper definition of what it defines as harmful, however, iCloud users are essentially left at Apple’s mercy: If it chooses to continue to bend the knee to the Trump administration, for example, content deemed objectionable by the standards of political figures could end up wiped out. Apple also hasn't explained whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will be responsible for identifying and removing so-called harmful content, or whether any decisions will be left to AI, which can easily be fooled into making a bad moderation call. The scanning of such content, as mentioned above, begins with version 27.3 of Apple’s various OSes, which were released to developers in beta on Tuesday, with a general release expected in December. Apple didn’t respond to questions for this story. ®

technology.title: AMD's record quarter: Data center business doubles, while gaming craters
technology.description: AMD reported third-quarter revenues on Tuesday with a record $13.4 billion, an increase of 45 percent year over year, as data center business nearly doubled and the company's gaming segment cratered. AMD CFO Jean Hu said, "We expect revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The middle point of our guidance represents approximately 66% year-over-year revenue growth, primarily driven by the acceleration of our Data Center segment." AMD says its Q4 revenue projections are up another 27 percent from this quarter's results. As reported by Tom's Hardware , Intel's Q4 guidance places revenue estimates between $15 and $16 billion. That means that if both companies land where they expect to at the end of the fourth quarter, AMD would exceed Intel's revenue for the first time in history. The data center segment of AMD's business was up 97 percent year over year, with a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes the growth to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs, along with the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs . Sales of AMD Ryzen mobile chips led growth in the Client business, which includes desktop Ryzen processors and posted $2.95 billion in revenue, up 7 percent year over year. technology.title: Hey, Siri: Plug into my app like you said you'd do way back in 2024
technology.description: As of Tuesday, developers can explore expanded Siri AI integration for their Apple platform apps through beta releases of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3. Next spring, nearly three years after announcing plans for deeper third-party Siri integration, Apple expects to begin accepting App Store submissions using the new capabilities. "This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers," Apple said in a developer news post . "With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers." Anything is likely to be an improvement. Apple's Siri, a voice-activated assistant service, dates back to 2011 and gained limited third-party app access in 2016. In 2024, it became an interface for interacting with Apple Intelligence, its suite of generative AI features. Apple Intelligence has not been very intelligent – several advertised Siri capabilities were delayed, so much so that Apple was sued in 2025 over allegations of misleading marketing. After a shakeup of Apple's machine learning group in December 2025, Siri and Apple Intelligence received a makeover at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference in June. "Before this year, Siri was a timer with a voice," said Roberto Gutierrez, Apple platforms staff engineer at a media company and author of the e-book On-Device Intelligence, in an email to The Register . "Weather, alarms, calls. Anything past that was a coin toss. "On the developer side, SiriKit covered a handful of domains and Shortcuts only worked if users memorized the phrase. Siri AI is the first version that understands context and can chain actions across apps. That's a real change." There is a catch, however, Gutierrez observed. Siri AI is available in a limited number of languages and regions. Support for Traditional Chinese is expected by the end of 2026, and EU availability remains a matter of negotiation – Siri AI is unavailable on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS in the bloc as Apple works through interoperability concerns under Europe's Digital Markets Act. "Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," the company said last month without committing to any concessions. Gutierrez said that he expects opening Siri to third-party developers will be useful to some extent. "Siri can only do what apps expose through App Intents, and SiriKit is on its way out," he said. "If your app's main actions aren't exposed, the new Siri can't see you. The bigger shift is letting Claude, Gemini and others plug in. Developers already choose between three options for every AI feature: Apple's system model, an open model through MLX, or a cloud API. Siri is heading the same way. It doesn't need to be the smartest model. It needs to be the best router. That's the right call." technology.description: Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US. technology.title: Fedora 45 is finally finished and fit
technology.description: Fedora 45 is here , after not one but two week-long delays as the team found last-minute issues. Although both the original and second announcements were irksomely non-specific, in general we prefer this "when it's ready" approach to the rigid calendar-based schedule that Canonical favors for Ubuntu. It includes six main editions, five immutable desktop variants, and 12 "spins" with different GUIs. The combined version 45 release notes detail some of the bigger individual component changes and note the hardware requirements. The recommended spec is now a 2 GHz quad-core CPU with 8 GB of RAM and 20 GB of disk space, and at least 1024×768 graphics. Fedora 45 supports most display adapters, but 3D acceleration may not work on older GPUs, including Intel models prior to GMA9xx, Nvidia models prior to NV30 (GeForce FX5xxx series), and AMD Radeon models prior to R300 (Radeon 9500). We took a quick look at the beta back in September, focusing on its new next-generation text console, which is a welcome change. We especially liked the ability to zoom in and out on the text console on the fly, which is something we've missed since the superb "Laptop Ultravision" for DOS , about a third of a century ago. (The company is long gone, but we found a downloadable version for all you DOS users .) The desktop flagship editions are Workstation 45 , which comes with GNOME 51 "A Coruña" , and Fedora KDE Plasma Desktop , with KDE Plasma 6.8 . We covered some of the new features in GNOME 51 when we looked at the Ubuntu 26.10 beta , and those changes apply here too – notably, improvements in the Settings app, but removal of some older Nvidia GPU support. Both the big names are Wayland-only environments now, but by our reckoning, X11 fans have seven of the 12 official spins to choose from: Xfce, Cinnamon, MATE, i3, LXQt, LXDE, and Sugar (SOAS) all still use X.org if you prefer. There is also a combined What's New page for all the Atomic Desktops, Fedora’s immutable variants – the main shared feature here being the new web-based installer. The new version of main Fedora is accompanied by Fedora Asahi Remix 45 for Apple Silicon Macs. This is a more notable release than the cross-platform editions, as Asahi 45 brings initial support for M3-based Macs as well as M1 and M2 kit. As The Reg described in September , though, the M3 support is preliminary and limited – for instance, it excludes the M3 Ultra. If you have an M3 Mac, for now, you're better off sticking to macOS. The most important changes in Fedora 45 are under the hood, which is what the Red Hat release announcement focuses on. It now uses RPM version 6.1, with enhanced package signature checking , and blocks the vendor of packages silently changing. The GNOME keyring now uses the oo7 secrets manager . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
science.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

science.title: Trump declares 'American space superiority for all eternity' in election night proclamation
science.description: null President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws. "The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars , but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives. "Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says. Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity." "The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization. The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth . The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit . Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030. Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

science.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) In an update on Oct. 23, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders shared the agency’s path to returning Americans to the lunar surface in 2028. Agency leadership provided updates on the previously announced acceleration plans for the Artemis program, advancing toward the agency’s Artemis III test flight in 2027 and Artemis IV Moon landing mission in 2028. Building on the priorities announced at Ignition earlier this year, NASA leadership shared the agency’s significant progress across its missions, working with industry partners to test critical capabilities, reduce risk, and build toward a sustained American presence on the Moon. This graphic shows NASA’s concept of operations for Artemis III. The mission will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings. NASA “This is a very energized NASA, and these updates are only a small part of that story. We are bringing extreme focus to the mission to ensure delivery of world-changing outcomes as quickly, safely, affordably, and successfully as possible,” said Isaacman. “NASA is driving outcomes to make Moon missions a reality, and we’re not waiting for others to bring their plans to us — the campaign must move with urgency as strategic competitors pursue a permanent presence beyond Earth.” The agency shared details of the Artemis III mission, which will test rendezvous, docking, and operations between NASA’s Orion spacecraft and lunar lander test vehicles from SpaceX and Blue Origin in Earth orbit. science.title: 'Trials and Tribble-ations' at 30: The classic 'Star Trek: Deep Space Nine' episode that brought Captains Kirk and Sisko face-to-face
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

When "Star Trek" celebrated its 60th anniversary in September, it was a strangely muted affair. Sure, there were fan events, screenings, and even an attempt at a world record for the biggest simultaneous Vulcan salute in history , but the lack of a "Doctor Who"-style birthday episode felt like a glaring omission. It was like everyone had shown up for the party, but the organizers had forgotten to book the headline entertainment. Luckily, there were rather more fireworks for the show's 30th birthday, when both "Voyager" and "Deep Space Nine" marked the occasion in style. "Voyager" episode "Flashback" took Tuvok (Tim Russ) back to his days on the USS Excelsior bridge alongside Original Series vets Hikaru Sulu (George Takei) and Janice Rand (Grace Lee Whitney). But it was "DS9"'s "Trials and Tribble-ations" that turned out to be the more memorable voyage to "Trek" past, as Captain Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) — with the help of some then-state-of-the-art digital trickery — came face-to-face with a young Captain James T. Kirk (William Shatner). While "Flashback" aired within days of "Trek"'s September 8 birthday, fans had to wait a little longer for "DS9"'s contribution to the celebrations. Showrunner Ira Steven Behr was keen to avoid disrupting the space station-set drama's story arc for a comedic diversion, meaning that "Trials and Tribble-ations" didn't debut until November 4, 1996. In the wake of "Flashback" — not to mention Spock and Scotty's comebacks in "The Next Generation" stories "Unification" and "Relics" — the "DS9" writers' room had already decided they needed to take a very different approach. science.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100. Swift — officially known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer — launched to Earth orbit in November 2004 on a two-year mission to study gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the most powerful explosions in the universe . "Swift" was not an acronym but rather referred to the spacecraft's observational agility. "Swift needed to detect and locate gamma-ray bursts, communicate their position to other observatories, and then swing its telescopes around to image the burst locations before their afterglows faded out," S. Bradley Cenko, Swift's principal investigator (PI) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, said in an Oct. 23 statement . "This typically took Swift about a minute to do." Swift didn't just observe GRBs. It also studied a variety of other cosmic bodies and phenomena, from faraway supernova explosions and feeding black holes to asteroids and comets in our own solar system. And it kept doing this long after its warranty expired — for about 20 years after, in fact. The space telescope didn't conduct its final science observation until this past Oct. 20 . (Swift underwent a name change during this stretch: In 2018, it was rechristened the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after its first PI, who died the previous year.) "Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of NASA's Astrophysics Division, said in the same Oct. 23 statement. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," he added. (Image credit: Katalyst Space)) Swift was incredibly productive, observing more than 2,000 GRBs and 1,400 supernovas over the course of its long scientific life. But it could have gathered even more data, had a dramatic rescue mission worked out. science.title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
science.description: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes. When put to the test, it led to more than twice the reduction of plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding as conventional toothbrushes. “The concept is great,” says Nicholas Jakubovics at Newcastle University, UK, who wasn’t involved in the research. “Basically, the mechanical forces recharge the surface, so it’s really innovative. Anything that even slightly improves the way dental care works could have a benefit, because oral disease is just so widespread.” Read more How regrowing your own teeth could replace dentures and implants Oral diseases, such as tooth decay, affect nearly half the global population . Brushing regularly can help remove plaque, a sticky layer of bacteria that forms on teeth. These bacteria can produce acids that cause cavities and irritate gums, sometimes leading to tooth loss. Advertisement But even thorough brushing can leave behind bacteria deep in plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to grow back within hours. Researchers have previously developed toothbrushes with antibacterial metal nanoparticles, including silver and zinc, embedded in their bristles , although their long-term effectiveness is uncertain. Others have designed ionic toothbrushes that use electric currents to help loosen plaque , but they are dependent on batteries. Now, Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China and her colleagues have turned to studies showing that so-called piezoelectric materials fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants. These generate electric charges under pressure , prompting Lu’s team to develop toothbrush bristles made from piezoelectric plastic. The researchers made two sets of bristles of different thicknesses, both of which met Chinese national standards for softness and strength. Laboratory tests confirmed the bristles generated electricity under pressure, particularly the thicker ones. The team also detected reactive-oxygen species on the brushes, which remained soft and retained their electrical properties after three months of use. science.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
science.description: null Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons. While the latter is the tallest volcano in the solar system, at 374 miles (600 km) across, about the size of Arizona, the Alba Mons region is the largest volcano when considering surface area. TGO detected gas containing hydrogen chloride making its way to the surface of Mars through the Alba Mons fissures. The same gas is commonly found escaping from magmatic vents on Earth, with the compound coming from hot magma beneath the surface. Detecting it on Mars is a sign of dormant Martian volcanism. Orbital imagery had previously shown some volcanoes appear to have been active within the last few million years, and seismometers have detected the rumbling of "marsquakes," both implying the Red Planet is volcanically active. However, eruptions and lava flows have been conspicuous by their absence. "Our findings suggest that Mars has retained enough internal heat to support volcanic activity until recently, and possibly still does," team co-leader and scientist at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Daniel Mège, said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "The TGO was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack." Evidence of dormant Martian volcanism is rising Mège and colleagues were first alerted to something strange happening on Mars when they noticed spikes of hydrogen chloride during Martian summer and on the northern hemisphere of the Red Planet. That is both a time and place at which hydrogen chloride shouldn't be detected. The gas usually peaks in the northern hemisphere during winter on Mars, disappearing in the summer. This variation is connected to the water and dust cycle on Mars. An exception to the rule occurs over volcanic fissures on the flanks of the Alba Mons volcano, in early summer. The TGO followed up on this by detecting fresh and narrow fissures, in some cases hundreds of feet long, in the Alba Mons region. A clear sign of volcanism. "It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere," Mège said. science.title: NASA Announces Ka-Band Satellite Relay Awards for Space Communications
science.description: Credit: NASA NASA selected three companies on Wednesday to perform work to develop Ka-band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space, ensuring service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. Through this work, NASA will aim to acquire end-to-end solutions that include space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements, as one of many customers in the commercial marketplace. The awards, under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E, are firm-fixed-price contracts that give NASA the option to provide additional funding up to the award limit to advance from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in-orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from Nov. 4 through May 3, 2027, with additional priced options to continue work through 2029. The contract awardees with maximum potential value inclusive of all future options are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million. Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million. Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. Facilitated through the agency’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project, this work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. In addition to the commercial capabilities currently under development by the program’s industry partners, Ka-band services are needed to support select in-orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non-compatible commercial services. A dyslexia diagnosis can help struggling children, but what about the rest?
science.description: Shutterstock/Jakub Krechowicz In years gone by, children who struggled to learn to read and spell were labelled “stupid”, “lazy” or “dim”. Today, of course, we are much more enlightened – now we label many of these children as “dyslexic”. But perhaps this label is still a bad idea. Picture two 9-year-olds reading at the level of an average 6-year-old. One gets a diagnosis of dyslexia. This positively affects her wellbeing. Her teachers now understand she has dyslexia and that she can get tailored help. The other child isn’t so lucky. Maybe his parents can’t afford a dyslexia test – in the UK, assessment isn’t available on the NHS and can cost several hundred pounds. In the US it could set parents back thousands of dollars. Or perhaps he was tested but the result was negative. Until very recently, this outcome was common for already disadvantaged children, because the official definition of dyslexia included the idea of “discrepancy” – that reading problems should be unexpected given a child’s other cognitive abilities. Assessing ability using IQ tests can also be biased against those from lower socioeconomic groups or learning to read in a second language. By extension, this second child is just bad at reading or lazy, or both, and not eligible to receive extra help with reading. Advertisement Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help, the other does not Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help and understanding and the other doesn’t, all because of a label. Yet this label is based on a questionable assessment. Despite trials using a wide range of cognitive processes, researchers have been unable to find meaningful ways to identify dyslexia. So, why not just help all children who struggle to read? Each has a unique combination of risk and remediation factors, but all will benefit most if we intervene when the problem first shows up, instead of waiting years for them to fail and then receive a diagnosis. Our newfound understanding of what is happening in their brains even suggests some surprisingly simple ways to help . Giving every child the best possible chance to overcome their challenge is what matters, not the label we attach to them.

science.title: The DNA is backwards on The Selfish Gene’s cover – again
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Don’t get it twisted Feedback is not young. We have been here on the back pages for many years, endlessly pushing a boulder up a hill and trying to take joy in the effort. This means, every so often, we are forced to repeat ourselves – because the world repeats itself. With a due sense of ennui, we turn our world-weary eyes to the cover of the new 50th anniversary edition of Richard Dawkins’s popular science classic The Selfish Gene . The title, written in all-caps, takes up most of the cover. The “I” in “SELFISH” has been replaced by a colourful little drawing of a DNA double helix. Advertisement Alas, something is awry. Geneticist Simon Fisher pointed it out on Bluesky : “You know a gene is selfish when its DNA twists the wrong way, as demonstrated by the left-handed double-helix proudly adorning the 50th Anniversary Edition of the multimillion copy bestseller on this topic.” Yes, once again we have an example of a DNA molecule being drawn, essentially, backwards. In reality, it is a right-handed double helix, but the one on the book cover is left-handed. It’s twisting the wrong way. Feedback’s mind’s eye immediately cast itself back to March 2025 , when we covered a Lego model that included many scientific and technological objects, including a sadly left-handed DNA. It turns out that The Selfish Gene ‘s art has been wrong for at least a decade. Patrick Goymer , an editor at PLOS One , shared the cover of the 40th anniversary edition on Bluesky, and it has the same left-handed DNA in place of the “I”. Feedback notes that our own copy is the 30th anniversary edition, and the DNA is correct. At some point since 2006, the DNA on the cover has flipped into a mirror universe. This little mistake would be doubly embarrassing if, say, the Nobel prize in chemistry had recently been awarded for research into these sorts of mirror molecules. Can you imagine? Coca-Cola faecaloma Sometimes a scientific paper has a title so vivid, so immediate, that Feedback just has to write about it. Such is the case with a paper published in Cureus , titled: “Massive fecaloma dissolved by Coca-Cola: A case report”. It was sent to us by Australia reporter Alice Klein, who either has a truly terrible browser history or makes extensive use of a VPN. A faecaloma, for those not yet blessed with the knowledge, is a large lump of impacted faeces trapped in a person’s rectum. In this case report, the faecaloma had a maximum diameter of 12.2 centimetres.
